src/infrastructure/TaskController.ts add(): inline dueDate type check (allows null, unlike optionalString); file-local queryString() validates req.query values that may be arrays. Both are minor local variants, not clear duplication of an httpSupport rule
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is a single infrastructure adapter layer. It holds in-memory repositories that implement domain ports, a UUID generator that implements the application's IdGenerator port, Express controllers that share httpSupport helpers, one error-to-status mapper (errorMiddleware), and the startup wiring (createApp/server). All of it adapts the core to concrete technology. The abstractions are used consistently: every controller uses asyncHandler, bodyOf and requiredString/optionalString; error-to-status mapping happens only in errorMiddleware; the repositories follow the same Map-based pattern. TaskController has two small local validations: an inline dueDate check that also allows null, and a file-local queryString helper for req.query values. Each has slightly different semantics from the httpSupport helpers, so neither is clear duplication or bypass. They are minor candidates to move into httpSupport, not material violations.
